title: Segment
description: One named slice of what an organisation serves: a level, a region, a product line, a service tier. Segments are what a gap is observed in and what a measure is broken down by, and they are a tree rather than two kinds — a dimension is simply a Segment with no parent, and its values are its children, the same shape Goal already uses for its levels. So "geography" is a Segment and "the northern region" is its child, without a second kind for regions. Not a BeneficiaryGroup: a group is who work is for, a segment is where a shortfall was observed, and a region or a service tier is not a group of people. See GAP_DESIGN.md.

parent.description: The dimension this is a value of, or the broader slice it sits inside. Absent for a dimension itself. A kind rule refuses a segment that is its own ancestor.

description.description: What falls inside this slice and what does not, precisely enough that two people counting it would agree.
